variables_and_units.primary_outcome: Mean of T3 and T7 temperature in degrees C at +30, +40, and +50 minutes relative to the mean at -30, -20, and -10 minutes.
variables_and_units.covariates: Pre-event mean T3/T7 in degrees C, T6 in degrees C, T_out in degrees C (airport-derived and partly interpolated), clock time, and weekday.

candidates.testable_prediction: Among isolated high single-interval events defined before outcome inspection, the matched event-minus-control T3/T7 change over +30 to +50 minutes will be positive, with a day-block 95% interval excluding zero, while the pre-event placebo will be near zero. This is an uncomputed hypothesis.
candidates.alternative: Any apparent delayed response is due to weather or time-of-day structure, reverse timing, sensor aggregation, selection, or unrelated indoor gains; alternatively, heterogeneous load sources produce no stable thermal signal.
candidates.discriminating_test: First preregister an isolation rule and threshold for one Appliances interval, then count eligible events without relaxing it. If enough events exist, match to low-load intervals on weekday, clock time, pre-event T3/T7, lights, T6, and T_out using fixed calipers; require complete contiguous windows. Estimate paired post-event and lead-placebo contrasts with event-day block uncertainty. If eligible event counts remain too small, stop the retrospective analysis and run prospective synchronized measurement with room-level submeter Wh, appliance on/off labels, and room temperatures in multiple homes.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Unknown for the revised single-interval definition because it was not computed. The prior sustained-event definition is infeasible in the broker result. The available columns could support a retrospective test if the revised rule yields enough eligible isolated events, but any result would remain a single-house observational association.
candidates.required_new_data: For monitoring validation, collect synchronized room-level plug/submeter Wh, appliance on/off labels, and room temperature at ten-minute or finer resolution in multiple homes. Predefine isolated-event thresholds, alert precision or sensitivity/specificity, and matched low-load controls.
candidates.failure_condition: Reject the monitoring signal if the revised exposure has too few eligible events for the prespecified analysis, the matched post-event contrast is non-positive or its event-day interval includes zero, the lead placebo is comparably positive, or the direction fails a preregistered threshold sensitivity.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query on residential appliance-energy event detection using indoor temperature sensors, lagged thermal response, and submeter ground truth. candidates.title: Zone-specific thermal coupling as an operational ventilation-change monitor
candidates.question: Do zone-specific lags between north-side outdoor T6 and indoor temperatures T1-T9 reveal periods of increased indoor-outdoor thermal coupling that merit ventilation or envelope inspection?
candidates.new_claim: Input-level increment: evaluate a change-point monitor based on zone response lag to measured north-side outdoor temperature, then validate whether it corresponds to window or ventilation state. The data do not directly measure window opening or building heat loss.
candidates.input_delta: The data include indoor temperatures by named room, north-side outdoor T6, and airport T_out with some interpolation. The proposed target is changing zone-specific response lag, not aggregate energy prediction.
candidates.domain_value: A validated flag could direct an energy team to inspect unusual ventilation or envelope conditions before interpreting consumption changes as occupant behavior.
known_basis_refs: materials.official_documentation.variables: T1-T9 are room-specific temperatures; T6 is outside on the north side; T_out is airport weather.
materials.official_documentation.additional_info: room temperature/humidity observations were averaged over ten-minute periods; hourly airport weather was interpolated.
materials.case.unit: single house with no direct occupancy or appliance-switching measurement.
assumptions: T6 and indoor sensors are sufficiently synchronized to estimate lag at ten-minute resolution.
Rapid zone response can arise from ventilation or envelope coupling, but solar gains, internal heat, sensor placement, and other causes are alternatives.
Enough independent outdoor-temperature transitions exist to assess feasibility; unknown until computation.

variables_and_units.input: T6 and T_out, degrees C at ten-minute intervals.
variables_and_units.response: T1-T9, degrees C at ten-minute intervals.
variables_and_units.diagnostic: Zone-specific lag or response coefficient with a defined estimation window and uncertainty.
variables_and_units.validation_target: Window/ventilation state and HVAC state, measured prospectively; neither is supplied.

candidates.testable_prediction: Candidate periods with shorter T6-to-indoor response lag in one zone will be associated with independently logged window/ventilation changes there, compared with matched periods without such changes.
candidates.alternative: Lag shifts reflect seasonal drift, airport interpolation, indoor gains, sensor placement, or autocorrelation rather than ventilation or envelope state.
candidates.discriminating_test: Assess lag stability in blocked time segments using available sensors, then prospectively compare flagged and unflagged ten-minute windows against window contacts and HVAC logs, with sensitivity and false-alert rate fixed in advance.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Descriptive lag stability is testable; identifying ventilation events or diagnostic accuracy is impossible without state labels.
candidates.required_new_data: Window-contact and HVAC on/off logs, plus repeated measurements in several homes and zones, synchronized with T6, T_out, and T1-T9.
candidates.failure_condition: Reject the monitor if estimated lag shifts are not reproducible across blocked periods or do not predict logged state changes above a prespecified baseline alert rate.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query to test proximity: residential window opening detection from indoor-outdoor temperature time series and zone thermal response.

candidates.title: Persistent overnight appliance energy as a standby-load audit trigger
candidates.question: Does aggregate Appliances energy persist overnight when lights are zero and measured room temperatures are stable, enough to justify a plug-level standby-load audit?
candidates.new_claim: Input-level increment: turn recurring low-activity overnight consumption into a defined audit trigger, separating an operational screening rule from an unsupported claim that the energy is standby consumption.
candidates.input_delta: The task identifies separately measured Appliances and lights energy at ten-minute cadence. The proposed use detects recurring overnight energy persistence and triggers submeters rather than fitting another aggregate predictor.
candidates.domain_value: A screening rule could prioritize homes or periods for plug-level auditing and potential standby-load reduction.
known_basis_refs: materials.official_documentation.variables: Appliances and lights are separate energy variables in Wh.
materials.official_documentation.additional_info: energy is logged at ten-minute intervals.
materials.data_profile: Appliances has supplied median 60 Wh; overnight-specific summaries are not supplied.
assumptions: Clock time defines an overnight window, but lights=0 and stable temperatures do not prove occupant absence or lack of active devices.
A persistent aggregate floor could include refrigeration, heating, or necessary loads and cannot be called standby without device measurements.

variables_and_units.energy: Appliances and lights, Wh per ten-minute interval.
variables_and_units.context: Timestamp and T1-T9, degrees C, used for a prespecified stable-temperature condition.
variables_and_units.audit_unit: Contiguous overnight episode and household, not independent ten-minute rows.

candidates.testable_prediction: A subset of overnight blocks with lights=0 and stable room temperatures will show recurring Appliances energy above the low-load floor on multiple nights; plug-level follow-up should identify a measurable, controllable portion.
candidates.alternative: Energy is necessary refrigeration/heating or unmeasured occupant/device use; the screening condition may not predict controllable standby energy.
candidates.discriminating_test: Estimate recurrence of the defined overnight condition in the current series, then instrument circuits with plug-level submeters for at least two weeks. Compare flagged and matched unflagged nights and quantify controllable Wh/day.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Recurrence of aggregate overnight patterns is computable, but occupancy absence and standby-device attribution are unobserved.
candidates.required_new_data: Plug-level Wh by device or circuit, occupancy/activity diary or sensor if making absence claims, and repeated nights across households.
candidates.failure_condition: Do not use the screen for standby-load interventions if flagged periods lack a reproducible controllable plug-level load above matched unflagged baseline.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query to test proximity: residential standby energy detection from smart meter load profiles, night baseload screening, and plug-level validation.

final_idea.title: Thermal after-response to isolated household energy spikes
final_idea.question: After an isolated high Appliances-energy interval, does a delayed temperature change in the laundry and ironing zones distinguish the event from matched low-load periods well enough to prompt monitoring review?
final_idea.new_claim: Input-level increment: test a lagged room-temperature contrast following isolated single-interval aggregate-energy spikes as a monitoring signal, rather than predicting the contemporaneous aggregate target. This is proposal-only; no empirical support or literature novelty is claimed.
final_idea.input_delta: The supplied task and dataset describe aggregate Appliances energy and room sensors but do not propose an event-triggered delayed thermal monitor. The original sustained-event rule produced zero eligible events at both preregistered thresholds; testing isolated single-interval spikes is a revised, uncomputed exposure definition.
final_idea.domain_value: If validated prospectively, a delayed zone-temperature response could flag aggregate energy spikes for review and guide where to install submeters. It would not identify a device or justify automated control.

A preregistered isolation rule can distinguish isolated spikes from sustained episodes; event count remains uncomputed.
Matching on clock time, pre-event thermal state, lights, and observed outdoor conditions reduces some alternative explanations but cannot remove residual confounding.
The independent uncertainty unit is event day within the single-house series; multiple homes are needed for generalization.

final_idea.alternative: Weather, time-of-day, reverse timing, sensor averaging, unrelated internal gains, or heterogeneous load sources explain any observed pattern.
final_idea.discriminating_test: Preregister threshold and an isolation/guard rule, count eligible events, then match to low-load controls under fixed calipers and compare the 30-50 minute post-event contrast with the same pre-event placebo. final_idea.feasible_with_current_data: Unknown for the revised exposure definition. The prior sustained-event contrast was not estimable. Any retrospective association would be single-house and noncausal.
final_idea.required_new_data: For monitoring validation, synchronized room-level plug/submeter Wh, appliance on/off labels, and room temperatures at ten-minute or finer resolution in multiple homes, plus a preregistered alert-performance target.
final_idea.failure_condition: Reject the signal if the revised definition yields too few events, the post-event contrast is non-positive or its day-block interval includes zero, the lead placebo is comparably positive, or threshold sensitivity reverses the direction.
final_idea.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query for residential load-event monitoring using delayed indoor temperature response and submeter or appliance-state validation; returned sources are adjacent, and do not establish whether this relation is already known.

final.what_changed: The original idea predicted a thermal response after sustained high load, defined as >100 Wh in two adjacent intervals with a >150 Wh sensitivity. The broker found zero events under both definitions, so the contrast and placebo were not estimated. I revised the exposure to isolated single-interval spikes, but that version has not been computed; its feasibility and prediction remain unknown.
final.what_is_known: The supplied series contains 19,735 ten-minute rows for one house with aggregate Appliances/lights energy and room temperature sensors. C1 executed successfully with no errors and returned zero events and zero matches at both thresholds; consequently it produced no effect estimate, interval, or placebo result. S1 returned eight Crossref records with limited coverage. One 2022 abstract describes an 11-home AC dataset with electrical current, manually tagged ON/OFF state, and indoor temperature/humidity, supporting adjacency between appliance-state and temperature measurement. Other returned titles concern NILM event detection. Titles alone do not establish findings. The exact proposed delayed thermal contrast was not verified as new or known.
final.what_is_new_hypothesis: Isolated high single-interval aggregate-energy spikes may precede a delayed T3/T7 temperature response that can serve as a review trigger, with little pre-event lead signal. This is a new-to-input test proposal, not a world-literature novelty claim.
final.falsifier: With enough preregistered isolated events, a non-positive post-event contrast, an event-day interval including zero, a comparably positive lead placebo, or reversal under the prespecified threshold sensitivity rejects the monitoring signal. Too few events falsifies retrospective feasibility under the chosen rule, not the general physical possibility.
final.minimum_next_test: Before inspecting temperatures, preregister the isolated-interval Appliances threshold and guard interval. Report eligible events and event days. If adequate, match each event to low-load controls on weekday, clock time, pre-event T3/T7, lights, T6, and T_out; estimate the +30 to +50 minute minus pre-event contrast and the -60 to -30 minute placebo, with event-day block uncertainty and one threshold sensitivity. If inadequate, collect synchronized room-level submeter Wh, appliance state, and T3/T7 in multiple homes and apply the same preregistered comparison.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The Crossref return includes NILM event-detection titles and an abstract describing a labeled AC electricity/state and indoor-temperature dataset. This establishes nearby measurement and event-detection work, not that those sources test the proposed aggregate-load-to-delayed-room-temperature contrast. Coverage is limited and no full-text novelty review was done.
final.novelty_status: Adds a specific event-triggered lagged thermal-monitoring question to the supplied regression-focused input. World-literature novelty is unresolved; no claim that this is the first such relation is supported.
final.limitations: Single household and short observation period; aggregate energy does not identify appliances or occupancy; weather is partly interpolated; no intervention or device-state data; revised event definition uncomputed; search is relevance-ordered Crossref metadata with limited coverage.

request.purpose: Check whether the preregistered matched lagged thermal contrast and lead placebo are estimable and directionally consistent in the supplied single-house series; return counts and day-level uncertainty, not a causal estimate.
request.model_spec: Main event: Appliances >100 Wh for at least two adjacent ten-minute rows; event time is run start; merge runs separated by one non-high row. Controls have Appliances <=100 Wh throughout +/-60 minutes. Match without replacement on same weekday, circular clock-time distance <=60 minutes, pre-event mean(T3,T7) difference <=1 C, and T6 and T_out differences <=2 C, selecting minimum standardized squared distance. Outcome is mean(T3,T7) at +30,+40,+50 minutes minus mean at -30,-20,-10 minutes; lead placebo is mean at -30,-20,-10 minus mean at -60,-50,-40. Require contiguous ten-minute rows and complete windows. Bootstrap paired contrasts after averaging within event day, 1000 resamples with seed 42. Repeat at >150 Wh as threshold sensitivity.

request.missing_relation: Whether prior residential energy-monitoring work has tested delayed indoor room-temperature responses after aggregate appliance-load events, especially against submeter or appliance-state ground truth, and whether this exact monitoring relation is already established.
request.query: ("appliance energy" OR "residential energy") AND ("indoor temperature" OR "room temperature") AND (event detection OR event monitoring OR submeter OR appliance state) AND (lag OR delayed response)
request.change_if_found: If returned records directly study the same lagged thermal signature with submeter or appliance-state validation, narrow the claim to this dataset and its prespecified T3/T7 contrast or withdraw the literature-novelty implication; if only adjacent prediction or non-thermal event detection appears, retain the input-level hypothesis while marking world-literature novelty unresolved.

sources.title: Residential electricity current and appliance dataset for AC-event detection from Indian dwellings
sources.original_abstract:
Abstract 
                   Air Conditioners (ACs) have become a major contributor to residential electricity consumption in India. Non-intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) can be used to understand residential AC use and its contribution to electricity consumption. NILM techniques use ground truth information along with meter readings to train disaggregation algorithms. There are datasets available for disaggregation, but no dataset is available for a hot tropical country like India especially for AC event detection. Our dataset’s primary objective is to help train NILM algorithms for AC event detection and compressor operations. The dataset comprises of home-level electrical current consumption and manually tagged AC ground truth (ON/OFF status) data at 1-min interval, indoor environment temperature and relative humidity readings at 5-min interval and dwelling, AC and household characteristics. The data was collected from 11 homes located in a composite climate zone-Hyderabad, India for 19 summer days (May) 2019. The dataset consists of 1.6 million data points and 450 AC cycles with each cycle having a runtime of more than 60 min (> 2000 compressor ON/OF cycles). Public availability of such a dataset will allow researchers to develop, train and test NILM algorithms that recognize AC and identify compressor operations.
